chapter: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
title: Europe tour impressions: countries, Paris and the waterfront
summary: Five or six weeks in Switzerland, Sweden, Belgium, France and Germany, with food, a Paris night club, Arthur Briggs and a wander through Marseilles waterfront with Cecil Payne.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: there for over a week...haha. We couldn't get out of the hotel, hahahaha.
But how long were you in Europe all together?
Ohh. I think it was about five or six weeks. Yeah.
Oh we went to Switzerland, we went to Sweden, Belgium and France, of course, and I think we did a date in Germany, yeah.
Could you sum up in some way the things that impressed you most when you first went to Europe?

Well, we were movin' so fast... I'll never forget one day I became exuberant and so I says, "Come on, Al McKibbon, let's go eat." And I ordered a whole lot of stuff and we all ate good and there was somebody else there and so when the tab come Al McKibbon says, "Man, my God man..." Hahahaha. But

the food was so good and then, at that time, the weather was warm and...oh, at first, we were staying at that very exclusive hotel and oh it was somethin'. It was so expensive we had to get out of there, so we moved to another, a little hotel on the side street. (laughter) But when I was there I went out one night and I caught Earl Hines...no, whad I do?... I went out one night and, who did I catch, somebody that'd been in Europe since the '20's, a trumpet player. I forget his name.* I had a good time jammin' with him and then we did the Ambassador, of course we did Salle Playel twice and we did the Ambassador, night club, and Earl Hines and...Louis was in town at the time and Earl Hines and Jack Teagarden come in and jammed at the Ambassador, a very exclusive club. And they had another band in there, a big band, and this trumpet player, he played just like Harry James. (laughter)
You played concert dates there, did you? Or did you play some club dates as well?
No, I was just sayin' the Ambassador Night Club, that was a night club gig. That was a week, I think. Then we did concerts all

through France, you know. That was the only night club that we played. And Lyon, Marseilles. I'll never forget Cecil Payne and I, I say "Look here man, I'm tired of sittin' in this hotel room," I said, "Let's go out." So we went all down in the water-front, just him and me. We wandered into all them places and so Cecil say, "I'm gettin' scared." I said, "Man, don't be scared." I didn't know the language but I could use my hands and my eyes and I could be understood. So we got over. (laughter) I say, "Let's go in this place." He say, "Nick, come on man." (laughter) I had a good time.
